title: Data Structures and Algorithms
tagline: The core of a computer-science degree, in C++
description: Lists, trees, graphs, hashing, sorting and dynamic programming, each built from scratch in C++ and then measured. You learn how to reason about running time, build every classic structure yourself, and choose the right one for a problem, finishing with a spelling checker built on a trie and edit distance. It assumes the first milestones of the C++ course: functions, classes, vectors, references and templates.

milestones.title: Complexity and Linear Structures
milestones.blurb: Big O and how to reason about running time, measuring real programs, dynamic arrays, linked lists, and stacks, queues and deques.

lessons.title: Complexity and Big O
lessons.summary: How to describe an algorithm's speed independently of the computer - counting basic steps, Big O and its relatives Omega and Theta, the common growth classes, analysing sequential, nested and halving loops, best, worst and average cases, amortised cost, and space complexity.

lessons.title: Measuring Real Performance
lessons.summary: Turning theory into measurements - timing code with std::chrono, avoiding the traps of optimisation and noise, doubling experiments that reveal the growth class, how the memory hierarchy and cache lines make some O(n) loops much faster than others, and when constant factors matter.

lessons.title: Dynamic Arrays
lessons.summary: How std::vector works inside - a contiguous block with a size and a capacity, growth by doubling and why it gives amortised O(1) push_back, the cost of inserting and erasing in the middle, building a small vector class with a rule-of-five, and what invalidates iterators.

lessons.title: Linked Lists
lessons.summary: Nodes connected by pointers - singly linked lists with push_front, insertion after a node and reversal, owning nodes with std::unique_ptr, doubly linked lists with a sentinel, the costs compared with a vector, std::list and std::forward_list, and the two-pointer techniques for finding the middle and detecting a cycle.

lessons.title: Stacks, Queues and Deques
lessons.summary: The restricted containers - stacks (last in, first out) for undo, matching brackets and evaluating expressions, queues (first in, first out) built as ring buffers, deques open at both ends, the standard adapters std::stack, std::queue and std::deque, and the monotonic-deque trick for sliding-window maximums.

milestones.title: Searching and Hashing
milestones.blurb: Binary search and its variants, hash functions, hash tables with chaining and with open addressing, and choosing the right container.

lessons.title: Binary Search and Its Variants
lessons.summary: Finding things in sorted data in O(log n) - the halving idea, writing binary search without off-by-one bugs using half-open ranges and invariants, lower and upper bounds, std::lower_bound, upper_bound and equal_range, searching a rotated array, binary search on the answer, and searching over real numbers.

lessons.title: Hash Functions
lessons.summary: Turning keys into numbers - what a hash function must and should do, from keys to bucket indexes, why naive hashes cluster, polynomial string hashing, FNV-1a, std::hash and how to hash your own types, combining hashes, collisions and the birthday paradox, and hash flooding attacks.

lessons.title: Hash Tables with Chaining
lessons.summary: The classic hash table - an array of buckets, each holding a chain of entries, insert, find and erase, the load factor and why the expected chain length stays constant, rehashing by doubling, how std::unordered_map is built and its bucket interface, reserve and max_load_factor, and the worst case.

lessons.title: Open Addressing
lessons.summary: Hash tables that keep entries directly in the array - linear probing, why erasing needs tombstones (or backward-shift deletion), primary clustering and the expected probe counts, quadratic probing and double hashing, keeping the load factor below about 0.7, Robin Hood hashing, and power-of-two tables with a mixing step.

lessons.title: Choosing a Container
lessons.summary: Matching the data structure to the job - the costs of the standard containers side by side, ordered versus unordered maps and sets, sorted vectors and flat maps, multisets and multimaps, problems solved by the right container (counting, grouping, first-unique, longest consecutive run), and a checklist for choosing.

milestones.title: Sorting and Heaps
milestones.blurb: Insertion and selection sort, merge sort, quicksort, binary heaps, priority queues and heapsort, and counting and radix sort.

lessons.title: Insertion and Selection Sort
lessons.summary: The simple quadratic sorts and what they teach - selection sort, insertion sort and why it is fast on nearly sorted data, inversions as a measure of disorder, stability, sorting in place, comparators and strict weak ordering, and why real libraries still use insertion sort for small pieces.

lessons.title: Merge Sort
lessons.summary: Divide and conquer - merging two sorted halves in linear time, top-down merge sort and its recursion tree, the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n and the master theorem in practice, stability and the extra buffer, bottom-up merge sort, counting inversions while merging, and the Ω(n log n) lower bound for comparison sorting.

lessons.title: Quicksort
lessons.summary: Sorting by partitioning - the Lomuto and Hoare partition schemes, quicksort's average O(n log n) and worst-case O(n²), choosing pivots at random or by median of three, three-way partitioning for many duplicates, recursing on the smaller side, introsort (std::sort), and quickselect and std::nth_element for the k-th smallest element in linear time.

lessons.title: Heaps and Priority Queues
lessons.summary: The binary heap - a complete tree stored in an array, sift-up and sift-down, push and pop in O(log n), building a heap in O(n), heapsort, std::priority_queue and the heap algorithms, min-heaps with std::greater, and classic uses - top k, merging k sorted lists, and the running median with two heaps.

lessons.title: Counting and Radix Sort
lessons.summary: Sorting without comparisons - counting sort for small key ranges and how prefix sums make it stable, radix sort digit by digit (least significant digit first) for integers and fixed-length strings, bucket sort for evenly spread values, when these linear-time sorts beat std::sort, and a summary of every sort in the milestone.

milestones.title: Trees
milestones.blurb: Binary trees and traversals, binary search trees, self-balancing AVL trees, Fenwick and segment trees, and union-find.

lessons.title: Binary Trees and Traversals
lessons.summary: Trees as recursive structures - nodes, roots, leaves, depth and height, binary trees with unique_ptr children, writing functions recursively (size, height, mirror), the depth-first orders pre-, in- and post-order, doing them without recursion using an explicit stack, level-order traversal with a queue, rebuilding a tree from two traversals, and serialising a tree to text.

lessons.title: Binary Search Trees
lessons.summary: Ordered binary trees - the search-tree property, search and insert in O(height), deleting a node with zero, one or two children, minimum, maximum, floor and ceiling, successors, range queries and counting, augmenting nodes with subtree sizes for rank and select, why insertion order can make the tree degenerate, and how std::set and std::map relate.

tasks.title: A search tree with rank and select

lessons.title: AVL Trees
lessons.summary: Keeping a search tree balanced - the AVL balance condition and why it bounds the height by about 1.44 log n, storing heights in the nodes, left and right rotations, the four imbalance cases (left-left, right-right, left-right, right-left), insertion with rebalancing on the way back up, deletion, and how AVL trees compare with red-black trees, treaps and B-trees.

lessons.title: Fenwick and Segment Trees
lessons.summary: Answering range questions on changing arrays - prefix sums and their weakness, the Fenwick (binary indexed) tree with its lowest-set-bit trick for O(log n) updates and prefix sums, segment trees for any associative operation such as minimum or maximum, building, point updates and range queries, and a first look at lazy propagation for range updates.

lessons.title: Union-Find
lessons.summary: Tracking groups that merge - the disjoint-set problem, a forest of parent pointers, find and union, union by size or rank, path compression, the nearly constant inverse-Ackermann bound, counting components and component sizes, and applications such as connectivity, image regions, percolation and (in lesson 5.04) Kruskal's algorithm.

projects.title: Range sums with a Fenwick tree

milestones.title: Graphs
milestones.blurb: Representing graphs, breadth- and depth-first search, topological order, Dijkstra's shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, and A* on grids.

lessons.title: Graphs and Breadth-First Search
lessons.summary: Modelling connections - vertices and edges, directed, undirected and weighted graphs, adjacency matrices, adjacency lists and edge lists with their costs, breadth-first search and why it finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs, rebuilding the path from parent links, connected components, two-colouring (bipartite graphs), grids as implicit graphs, and multi-source BFS.

lessons.title: Depth-First Search and Topological Order
lessons.summary: Going deep first - depth-first search recursively and with an explicit stack, discovery and finish order, finding cycles in directed graphs with three colours, directed acyclic graphs, topological sorting by DFS finish times and by Kahn's algorithm, using topological order for build systems, course prerequisites and longest paths, and a pointer to strongly connected components.

lessons.title: Shortest Paths with Dijkstra
lessons.summary: Shortest paths when edges have weights - why BFS no longer works, relaxation, Dijkstra's algorithm with a priority queue and lazy deletion, its O((V + E) log V) cost, rebuilding routes, why negative weights break it, Bellman-Ford and negative cycles, 0-1 BFS, and choosing the right shortest-path algorithm.

lessons.title: Minimum Spanning Trees
lessons.summary: Connecting everything as cheaply as possible - spanning trees, the cut property that makes greedy choices safe, Kruskal's algorithm with sorting and union-find, Prim's algorithm with a priority queue, the dense O(V^2) version of Prim for complete graphs, minimum spanning forests, and uses from network design to clustering.

lessons.title: Grid Search and A*
lessons.summary: Finding paths faster with a sense of direction - weighted grids, Dijkstra exploring in every direction, the A* algorithm with f = g + h, admissible and consistent heuristics (Manhattan, Chebyshev, octile, Euclidean), tie-breaking, comparing how many cells each algorithm expands, and where A* is used in games, robotics and puzzles.

milestones.title: Algorithm Design
milestones.blurb: Greedy algorithms, dynamic programming from memoisation to tables, the classic DP problems, tries and string matching, and backtracking.

lessons.title: Greedy Algorithms
lessons.summary: Building a solution one locally best choice at a time - when greedy works and how to prove it with an exchange argument, interval scheduling by earliest finish time, counting meeting rooms with a sweep, why greedy coin change fails for some coin systems, Huffman coding with a priority queue, the fractional knapsack, and a checklist for spotting greedy problems.

lessons.title: Dynamic Programming
lessons.summary: Solving problems by combining answers to overlapping subproblems - why naive recursion explodes, memoisation (top-down), tabulation (bottom-up), the recipe of state, transition, base cases and order, counting paths in a grid, minimum coins for any coin system, counting the ways to make change, rebuilding the chosen solution, and saving memory by keeping only the rows you need.

lessons.title: Classic Dynamic Programming Problems
lessons.summary: The problems every programmer meets - the 0/1 knapsack and why its one-row version loops backwards, the longest common subsequence (behind diff tools), edit distance (behind spelling correction and DNA alignment) with a one-row optimisation, and the longest increasing subsequence in O(n log n) with patience sorting.

lessons.title: Tries and String Matching
lessons.summary: Data structures and algorithms for text - tries for prefix lookups and autocompletion, the cost of naive substring search, the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm and its prefix function, Rabin-Karp with a rolling hash, what std::string::find and std::search do, and a glance at suffix arrays and Aho-Corasick for many patterns.

lessons.title: Backtracking
lessons.summary: Searching through every possibility, cleverly - the choose, explore, unchoose pattern, generating subsets, permutations and combinations, the N-queens puzzle with constant-time safety checks, solving Sudoku, pruning dead ends early, branch and bound, and a first look at NP-complete problems, where exhaustive search is the best known exact method.
